data.content_ref: inline:SRC_007 contradicts SRC_002 by inverting the directional assignment of the $10 premium: SRC_002 depends on N=P+10 (notebook above pen) yielding P=1.25, while SRC_007 assumes P=N+10 (pen above notebook) yielding P=11.25. Both share the mechanism of algebraic substitution into N+P=12.50 but differ in which variable receives the additive premium. This is refuted if the English sentence 'the notebook costs $10 more than the pen' is unambiguously parsed as N=P+10, or if the real-world implausibility of an $11.25 pen and $1.25 notebook is treated as a valid disqualifier.
